Corrective action should address ergonomic assessment and provision of mechanical handling aids for this repetitive task.

report_text: During valve replacement job on the 10-inch crude oil transfer line, the line was confirmed isolated and depressurised per the PTW. However, when the technician broke the flange on the bypass valve, residual crude oil (approx 200 litres) drained from a high point trapped section not captured in the isolation plan. The crude oil flooded the bunded area and splashed on the technician's coveralls. No ignition. No injury.
why_flagged_explanation: Residual trapped hydrocarbons released during a line-break despite a completed isolation sequence indicates the isolation plan failed to account for a high-point trap section. The 200-litre crude oil release and personnel contamination represents a credible ignition and flash fire SIF scenario that was averted only by the absence of concurrent ignition sources.
